overall: The AG found that the Select Board Vice Chair and a Housing Authority Vice Chair acting as a screening committee were a public body that violated the OML by meeting without notice or open session; it ordered compliance and minutes but declined to nullify the appointment.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged that the Select Board Vice Chair and a Housing Authority Board Vice Chair violated the OML by interviewing candidates outside a posted meeting to fill a vacancy.
allegations.key_passage: For all of these reasons, we find that the Screening Committee was a public body.

allegations.summary: The two Vice Chairs' candidate screening and interviews were held without posted notice and outside an open session accessible to the public.
allegations.key_passage: The Screening Committee violated the Open Meeting Law when, among other things, it failed to post notice of its meetings or convene in open sessions accessible to the public.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Select Board violated its own policies, precedent, and Town policies in the appointment process.
allegations.key_passage: The Division of Open Government’s review concerns compliance with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant asked that the Board redo the appointment process and nullify the appointment of the candidate selected to fill the seat.
allegations.key_passage: Although we find that the candidate screening was not performed in conformance with the Open Meeting Law, we decline to nullify the Select Board’s appointment.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law's requirements.
Within 60 days, the Screening Committee must create minutes of the meetings it held in screening candidates and certify to the AG's office that it has done so.
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Law’s requirements. We also order the Screening Committee within 60 days of the date of this letter, to create minutes of the meetings they held in their screening of candidates and to certify to our office that they have done so.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
